editorial:
Imagine waking up in a strange house with a bunch of strangers and realizing you cannot leave. You soon find out that there are weird machines attached to the back of your heads. These gadgets collect chemicals from your brain, but there is a catch: they only work when you feel intense pain. To get the doors to open, you and the other prisoners have to hurt yourselves or each other. It is a nasty, stressful setup that makes you wonder how far you would go just to get out of a room. The vibe is very tense, and you feel the panic as the characters realize they are trapped in a cruel game.

What really works here is how the movie handles the tension and the surprises. The acting feels real, and the way the characters turn on each other is scary because it feels possible. Some parts might feel a bit slow, but the payoff at the end is worth it. If you love movies that mess with your head, you should check this out.
endingExplained: You find out that the whole thing was a trick. The people were not actually trapped in a house; they were in a dream state caused by drugs. The machines were just a way to harvest their pain for a twisted experiment. In the end, the main character wakes up, but it is clear that the trauma from the experience will stay with them forever. The cycle of pain was just a game for someone else.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and twisted games.
